title: Massive Fire Erupts At World's Largest Oil Processing Plant In Saudi Arabia After Drone Attack | Video
summary: A drone strike on Saudi Aramco's Abqaiq facility and the East-West Pumping Station sparked a massive fire, confirmed by NASA FIRMS satellite imagery. Saudi authorities blamed Iran-backed groups in Iraq, began emergency flaring and warned they reserve the right to respond. The attack raises concerns over security of critical energy infrastructure and potential disruptions to global oil supplies, given Abqaiq processes a significant share of world crude.
content:
A massive fire broke out at Saudi Aramco's Abqaiq refinery after drones struck the facility and the East-West Pumping Station in Saudi Arabia. NASA FIRMS satellite imagery confirmed extensive fire activity at the site, indicating significant damage to one of the world's most important oil processing facilities.

Abqaiq is the world's largest crude oil stabilisation plant and processes between 5 and 7 per cent of global oil supply, making it a vital hub for international energy markets.

BREAKING: Saudi Aramco's Abqaiq refinery has been struck by drones, causing a massive fire at the facility and the East-West Pumping Station. NASA FIRMS satellite imagery confirms extensive fire activity at the site. Abqaiq is the world's largest crude oil stabilization plant,…pic.twitter.com/2pxF02N47C

— The Hormuz Letter (@HormuzLetter) July 27, 2026

Saudi Arabia has blamed Iran-backed resistance groups in Iraq for carrying out the attack. Following the strike, authorities began emergency flaring at multiple production sites as part of their response to the incident. The kingdom also said it reserves the right to respond to the attack.

The drone strike has raised concerns over the security of key energy infrastructure in the region, with the Abqaiq facility playing a central role in Saudi Aramco's oil processing operations.

Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry has urged Iraq's government to "take all necessary measures to prevent its territories from being used as grounds from which acts of aggression are launched." 

Satellite imagery has confirmed damage at the Abqaiq oil processing facility, a critical component of Saudi Aramco's operations and an important link in the global oil supply chain.

The facility processes a substantial share of Saudi Arabia's crude oil before it is exported, making it essential for maintaining global energy stability.

Aramco suspends production at Abqaiq and Riyadh after Houthi attack. Smoke seen over Al-Qatif.pic.twitter.com/pu298eYi6y

— Open Source Intel (@Osint613) July 27, 2026

The damage has sparked concerns over possible disruptions to oil supplies, which could place additional pressure on international energy markets.

Previous disruptions at the Abqaiq facility have had a significant impact on global oil prices, underlining the importance of the site to the world's energy network.

Saudi Arabia has maintained that it reserves the right to respond after blaming Iran-backed resistance groups in Iraq for the drone attack.

The facility processes a substantial share of Saudi Arabia's crude oil before it is exported, making it essential for maintaining global energy stability.
